facts.raw_span: 7-year history of a submucosal tumour below the esophagogastric junction
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen revealed a 70 × 50 × 55 mm hypoechogenic, subcardial mass on the posterior gastric wall
endoscopic evaluation demonstrated a recurrent bleeding tumour at the same site
resected endoscopically by a piecemeal technique under general anesthesia
7-year history of a submucosal tumour below the esophagogastric junction
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen revealed a 70 × 50 × 55 mm hypoechogenic, subcardial mass on the posterior gastric wall
endoscopic evaluation demonstrated a recurrent bleeding tumour at the same site
resected endoscopically by a piecemeal technique under general anesthesia

concepts.why: The patient has a submucosal tumour below the esophagogastric junction with histopathology confirming a lipoma.
The patient has a recurrent bleeding tumour at the same site after resection of a submucosal tumour, which could be indicative of a GIST.
The patient presents with melena, progressive anemia, and a hypoechogenic mass on the posterior gastric wall, which could be indicative of gastric adenocarcinoma.
The patient has a submucosal tumour below the esophagogastric junction with a recurrent bleeding tumour at the same site, which could be indicative of a leiomyoma.
The patient has a lipoma with a large size and a recurrent bleeding tumour at the same site, which could be indicative of a liposarcoma.

rationales.F02: Submucosal tumour below the esophagogastric junction is more typical of gastric lipoma, GIST, or leiomyoma.
rationales.F04: Melena is a non-specific symptom that can occur in various gastrointestinal conditions.
rationales.F07: A hypoechogenic mass on the posterior gastric wall is suggestive of a submucosal tumour.
rationales.F08: Histopathology confirmation of a lipoma strongly supports the diagnosis of gastric lipoma.
rationales.F09: Recurrent bleeding tumour at the same site suggests a possible malignant or benign tumour with high recurrence rate.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with melena, progressive anemia, and a recurrent bleeding tumor, along with the large size of the submucosal tumor, are more consistent with a GIST, which is a type of tumor known for its potential to cause bleeding and anemia, than with a benign gastric lipoma.
